output.name: Mivalun
output.myth: Aun built his second kite the winter after he cut the string. Ennu showed him how to bend the cane, and Aun sewed the cloth with his own sinew, trusting no other hands. It was the finest thing he ever made. He carried it to the high cliff to fly out after the first and bring it home. Tavo heard him from the Torn Sleeve, where he had torn Aun's good sleeve on a gull-stake, and laughed. The wind took the kite from his fingers before he found the spool. Hesk would not give him more string. She had counted every turn he made. So the second kite never left the ground. It hangs up there, unlit, its tail trailing toward the Iron Kettle, where the women of the cliff set the pot on the hearth and wait for boats that do not come. Sil saw it from the water and wept, and that is why her light is so pale. When a child is slow to come in from the wind, we say Aun's kite is waiting for someone to hold the spool.
output.finding: Start at Lutha, the Tallow Lamp, and go one fist and a little more to its west, where Mivalun hangs as a dim star in the Leeward Reach.
